newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-DEVILS TRADE CENTER BROTEN TO KINGS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-DEVILS TRADE CENTER BROTEN TO KINGS.

text.p: Centre Neal Broten, the last active member of the 1980 U.S. Olympic hockey gold medal team, was traded by the New Jersey Devils on Friday to the Los Angeles Kings for future considerations.
Broten, who had one assist in the Devils' first three games, had been assigned by New Jersey to the independent Minnesota Moose of the International Hockey League last week.
Devils general manager Lou Lamoriello said Broten, who turns 37 next week, no longer fits into the team's plans.
"Neal was an important part of our hockey team for a season-and-a-half," Lamoriello said.
"We appreciate everything Neal did for us in his short time insey. He is a true professional who deserves this chance to continue his hockey career."
New Jersey acquired Broten from Dallas in February 1995 and he scored the Stanley Cup-winning goal as the Devils completed an unlikely sweep of the Detroit Red Wings.
Broten has 281 goals and 623 assists in 1,060 NHL games.
The rebuilding Kings have three centres who are more than 30 years old in Broten, Ray Ferraro and Ed Olczyk. Los Angeles is 9-9-3 for 21 points, tied for third in the Pacific Division.
